title: ATE Rates and Honest Inference under Surrogate-Dependent Outcome Validation with Weak Overlap
banked_reason: Final D0.5 math and decision panels pass with no findings, but the cold general referee caps the achieved tier at subfield (paper score 7.1 below field cutoff 7.4) and marks the current scope not salvageable.
gap_reasons: The phase phenomenon is already established by Mou et al., and the new rate theorem is a specialized extension to general Hölder smoothness, unknown bounded design densities, binary outcomes, and the exact known validation protocol.

Its dyadic terms collapse algebraically to the ordinary sample variance of the truncated arm contrast, while the claimed strict length improvement is only against the deliberately loose Markov radius determined by C0, not against an optimal leading constant.
paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved matching risk and honest connected-interval length rates in the stated Hölder/Bernoulli model and added an observable studentized near-critical interval. The math and decision panels passed without findings; the cold general referee capped novelty at subfield because the phase diagram is known and the stronger interval comparison uses a loose Markov benchmark. A field-level continuation requires a separately scoped substantial result or re-anchor.
tldr: Primary outcomes in a randomized trial may be costly to validate even when a post-treatment surrogate is observed for everyone. Under the protocol-fixed law \(c_as^\kappa\), routine randomization identifies the full-population ATE, and the matched squared-error and honest-length rates are \(J_\kappa(h_n)/n\) and \(\sqrt{J_\kappa(h_n)/n}\). The field-level contribution is the fully observable near-critical inference theorem: a two-fold boundary-imputation center paired with a dyadic, covariance-corrected variance estimator is uniformly studentized for \(\kappa_n=1+t/\log n\), has infimal coverage \(1-\alpha+o(1)\), and has expected length uniformly strictly below the unclipped Markov-radius benchmark over the entire bounded near-critical class. Mou, Ding, Wainwright, and Bartlett retain credit for the weak-overlap phase phenomenon; the new claim is confined to this specified Holder, Bernoulli, unknown-random-design experiment and its connected interval.
gap: Robins et al. derive nuisance-smoothness minimax rates for missing-at-random means under response probabilities bounded away from zero, Khan and Tamer establish tail-driven irregularity of inverse-weighted parameters, and Mou et al. derive the exact weak-overlap phase calculation with a matching upper theorem for a first-order Sobolev reproducing-kernel Hilbert model. None gives an observable finite-sample estimator, same-class Bernoulli lower pair, or matched honest connected-interval expected-length frontier with constants uniform through \(\kappa=1\) for bounded unknown densities and Holder outcome regressions under the protocol-fixed spatial law \(c_as^\kappa\).
fill: Conditioning on the pre-specified protocol, the paper uses a boundary local average with a zero-count fallback, tail-mass-weighted imputation, and the known protocol weights to attain one integral frontier across all regimes. A reciprocal-power perturbation inside the same bounded-density, Holder-regression Bernoulli class matches the upper bound and transfers through two-point testing to every randomized connected interval.
